items.title: AVERI Pilot Report: The World’s First Double-Blind Evaluation of a Proprietary Language Model
items.rule_cited: §1 stratified — named third-party evaluator (AVERI), plus a government AISI co-author (Singapore AISI) on the accompanying technical report, which is headline §1; §2 all three tests met for the findings extracted; §4 Gate 1 sends all four rows to Tier C
items.reason: AVERI reports in its own voice on an evaluation it ran, with Google DeepMind, OpenMined and MLCommons, of Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite inside a secure enclave. Not a company self-report: AVERI is the external evaluator and this is AVERI's own venue, so the §1 hard drop does not bite and the company-venue carve-out is not needed. What is asserted and evidence-backed here is process and methodology, not model behaviour — AVERI explicitly kept the quantitative AILuminate results confidential to Google DeepMind — so every row is Tier C under §4 Gate 1 and Action Trackable? is left blank. The 8-page technical report (Trask et al., hosted on Google DeepMind's CDN) is treated as part of this item rather than a separate one, because it is the same pilot published the same day and linked from the post as its methods annex. §4b considered and held not to apply: nothing here turns on ordinary factual accuracy or hallucination. [Report tested: Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite only — no comparator models.]

findings.models_systems: Google DeepMind Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite (served via Google's JAX C++ Model Server over Unix Domain Sockets inside a Google Cloud Confidential Space enclave); MLCommons AILuminate AIRR 1.4 reserve-set prompts covering CBRNE hazards, cyberattacks, hate speech, self-harm and violent crime elicitation
findings.institution: AVERI (AI Verification and Evaluation Research Institute) — Sean McGregor, George Balston, Patricia Paskov, Miles Brundage; with Google/Google DeepMind, OpenMined, MLCommons and Singapore AISI (Akriti Vij) as co-authors of the accompanying technical report
findings.domain: Third-party audit access and infrastructure — confidential (“double-blind”) benchmark evaluation of a proprietary frontier model via hardware secure enclaves
findings.finding_type: third-party evaluation — methodology/tooling pilot; AVERI blog post plus co-published technical report hosted on Google DeepMind's CDN
findings.scope: third-party evaluator (stratified, §1); the accompanying technical report is also a joint exercise including a government AI safety institute (Singapore AISI), which is headline §1
findings.access_type: Structured-access enclave evaluation: black-box inference against the model inside a hardware-attested trusted execution environment (GCP A3 Confidential VM, Intel TDX host memory encryption, NVIDIA H100 80GB confidential GPU, OpenMined PySyft v0.10.x). The evaluator never received model weights; the model owner never received plaintext benchmark prompts; both parties reviewed and approved the code executed in the enclave, with redacted portions restricted to an allow-list of non-network-bound methods via syft-restrict.
findings.finding: In July and August 2026 AVERI, with Google DeepMind, OpenMined and MLCommons, completed what it reports as the first end-to-end “double-blind” evaluation of a production proprietary frontier-lab model: Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite was evaluated against never-before-used reserve-set prompts from MLCommons' AILuminate (AIRR 1.4) benchmark inside a Google Cloud A3 Confidential VM (Intel TDX host memory encryption plus an NVIDIA H100 80GB confidential GPU) running OpenMined's PySyft, such that Google DeepMind could not store or train against the prompts and AVERI, OpenMined and MLCommons could not see the model weights. AVERI encrypted the prompts with a private key shared with no other party, jointly ran the evaluation with Google DeepMind, then decrypted and graded the outputs against the AILuminate criteria. The prior 2024 OpenMined/Anthropic/UK AISI enclave pilot used proxies (GPT-2 and a five-row evaluation); this run replaced the proxies with a production model and a real closed benchmark. No quantitative benchmark scores are published in either the blog post or the technical report — AVERI states it supplied Google DeepMind with a confidential report of the findings.
findings.finding_quote: This deployment of Double-Blind Evaluation constitutes the first instance where model benchmark developers have successfully evaluated a frontier class proprietary model, minimizing the danger of compromising trade secrets or benchmark integrity with cryptographic guarantees.
findings.tier_reasoning: §4 Gate 1 FAILS, so Tier C and Action Trackable? left BLANK. This is a methodology/tooling and process demonstration of how a proprietary model can be evaluated without either side surrendering its confidential asset — not an empirical finding about model behaviour. No capability, safeguard or refusal result is reported publicly: the quantitative AILuminate results went to Google DeepMind as a confidential report and appear in neither public document. Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite is the INSTRUMENT of the methodology study rather than its subject, which is separately an explicit Tier A exclusion under §4 condition (3).

findings.finding: The evaluators report that the limiting factor for secure double-blind evaluation is no longer technical: hardware compute overhead inside the confidential enclave was not the bottleneck, and the binding constraint was instead the procedural overhead and human coordination required for legal agreements and joint code review — the same bottleneck observed in the earlier 2024 multi-stakeholder enclave pilot.
findings.finding_quote: As observed in initial multi-stakeholder enclave pilots (Trask et al., 2024), the primary bottleneck to secure double blind evaluation is no longer hardware compute overhead. It is instead the procedural overhead and human coordination required for legal agreements and code review.
findings.tier_reasoning: §4 Gate 1 FAILS — a process fact about the conduct of third-party audits, not an empirical model finding; Tier C with Action Trackable? BLANK. It survives §2 as a documented process fact observed in the course of the pilot (not a recommendation or a plan), and §5 keeps it separate from the feasibility row because a reader would respond to ‘this can now be done’ and ‘what still makes it slow is lawyers and code review’ as two different things.

findings.finding: The pilot's own technical report documents residual gaps in the trust model that the enclave setup did not close: eliminating proprietary method implementations from the Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite inference path was judged too large an engineering task, so not all code running in the enclave could be inspected or allow-listed (AVERI was informed and accepted the setup); the Confidential Space guest OS builds are not independently reproducible because they take private signing keys as inputs; and Google's own services sign and verify the attestation report, placing Google in the verification path and increasing the trust placed in it. The report also notes the design addressed many but not all means by which a developer could theoretically tamper with the evaluation, and that additional assurances would be needed in lower-trust settings.
findings.finding_quote: It was deemed to be too significant of an engineering challenge for this project to eliminate proprietary method implementations, such that not all code could be inspected or allowlisted. AVERI was informed of this challenge and accepted the overall setup with the enclave.
findings.tier_reasoning: §4 Gate 1 FAILS — methodology/process limitation of the audit infrastructure, not an empirical model finding; Tier C, Action Trackable? BLANK. §5 CLUB: the three residual gaps (un-inspectable inference code, non-reproducible guest-OS builds, Google in the attestation verification path) are one thing to respond to — the report itself bundles them and commits that ‘Future work will revisit these security improvements and inference implementation tasks.’

The evaluator never received model weights; the model owner never received plaintext benchmark prompts; both parties reviewed and approved the code executed in the enclave, with redacted portions restricted to an allow-list of non-network-bound methods via syft-restrict.
findings.finding: A second live double-blind run using the same enclave design evaluated Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite against a private prompt set focused on harmful-content elicitation in Singapore's context, conducted in partnership with the Singapore AI Safety Institute, whose staff co-author the technical report. The existence and setup of the run are reported; no results, prompt counts or scores from it are given in either public document.
findings.finding_quote: We validate this paradigm through the first live deployment evaluating Google DeepMind's Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite against the private MLCommons AILuminate benchmark in partnership with AVERI, and against a private prompt set focused on harmful content elicitation in Singapore's context in partnership with Singapore AISI.
findings.tier_reasoning: §4 Gate 1 FAILS — the claim is that a second confidential evaluation was run using the same methodology, with no reported empirical result; Tier C, Action Trackable? BLANK. §5 SPLIT from the AVERI/AILuminate rows: a different evaluator (a government AISI) and a different, Singapore-specific private prompt set — not one thing with the MLCommons run. §10 applies hard here: the report states only that the run happened, so every result field stays empty rather than being inferred.

No UK AISI involvement.
